misconception_description: Student believes that in the expression x == a or b, the comparison operator distributes to both operands of the or operator.

solutions.generated_code:
program HapusSpasi
kamus
  s, hasil : string
  i : integer
algoritma
  inputBaris(s)
  hasil <- ""
  for i <- 1 to panjang(s) do
    if s[i] != ' ' or 0 then
      hasil <- hasil + s[i]
    endif
  endfor
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student added input validation to check if the input is a string or list before processing. They believe the condition `type(text1) == str or list` checks whether the type is str OR whether the type is list. However, this is actually evaluated as `(type(text1) == str) or list`, and since `list` (the class object itself) is always truthy, this condition will always evaluate to True regardless of the input type. The student genuinely believes they are properly validating the input type and that this is a good defensive programming practice.
